Operational excellence including operator runbooks, simpler node configuration, observability and logging, and improved TUI

request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Hydra v2 production hardening and performance improvements across four workstreams: performance optimization, operational excellence, ecosystem support, and developer experience/maintenance.

claims.claim: Hydra is described as the only production-grade or production-ready Layer 2 scaling solution on Cardano.
Hydra is claimed to provide sub-second finality, near-zero or zero internal fees, high throughput, and L1-grade settlement guarantees.
The proposal states Hydra has powered or is used by Delta DeFi, Masumi, Hydra Doom, Glacier Drop, Intersect voting infrastructure, VTech Labs, Blockfrost, and Midgard.
The proposal claims Cardano L1 has over two hours of finality, approximately $0.17 payment fees, and roughly 7 to 10 TPS, making some high-performance applications uncompetitive on L1.
The proposal claims the requested funding will be milestone-gated with independent third-party assurance and Intersect administrative treasury governance.
The performance workstream targets 2x to 10x improvements in snapshot signing and memory profile and lower L1 fees through contract optimization.

Hydra activity is claimed to support treasury sustainability because head opening, fund changes, and closure create L1 transactions and fees, and some internal head fees could be routed to the L1 treasury on settlement.

The proposal claims Hydra advances treasury KPIs for TVL, monthly active users, monthly transactions, throughput capacity, reliability and uptime, and annual protocol revenue, and aligns with Pillars 1, 2, 4, and 5.
The proposal claims that if Hydra work slips, existing use cases risk migrating to competing chains and attracting new builders to Cardano will be difficult.
The proposal asks for ₳5,100,781 to deliver the described Hydra v2 workstreams.

summary: The anchor document requests ₳5,100,781 for Hydra v2 hardening and adoption work, asserting strong technical and ecosystem value but providing limited budget, feasibility, alternatives, failure-mode, and community-impact detail in the supplied text.
